newsitem.title: UK: Soco shares start trading at discount.
newsitem.headline: Soco shares start trading at discount.

text.p: Shares in UK oil and gas exploration company Soco International started trading on the London Stock Exchange on Thursday at a 6.5 percent discount to their placing price.
Soco, which was floated to raise to money for developing oil reserves in Mongolia primarily, traded at 243 pence in early afternoon business. The stocks had been placed at 260 pence a share.
"Initially there were two or three shareholders, who were disapointed at the absence of an initial premium and sold their shares," a market source said.
"But we are already seeing that other, more 'real' investors are buying those shares and taking up the flak in the after-market," this source added.
Turnover in Soco was 3.56 million shares.
Soco, which contains the international assets of Snyder Oil Corp from the U.S. and some interests from Cairn Energy Plc, placed 32.98 million shares to raise 85.7 million stg.
The money raised included 39.3 million of new money.
Besides Mongolia, Soco also has interests in Russia, China, Yemen, Thailand, Tunesia and Britain.
At a price of 143p per share, Soco's market capitalisation is about 114 million stg.
